claim.value: Brief customer follow-ups should document offline preparation and intended roster timing while explicitly identifying retrospective reports and unknowns.
claim.scope: Proposed supplementary data collection; reports are not presented as direct event-log observations.

provenance.rationale: The span supplies the collection method, subjects and epistemic labeling requirements.

signal_basis.value: Customer follow-ups produce documentation of reported offline preparation and intended roster timing, with retrospective reports and unknowns labeled and reported offline activity distinguished from logged events.
signal_basis.scope: Proposed supplementary documentation, assumed obtained for this assessment; no completed findings or verification of report truthfulness are implied.

provenance.rationale: These spans specify the follow-up documentation, distinction between reports and logs, proposed status, and limits on truthfulness.
The bounded documentation claim requires no unresolved empirical relation to supply its warrant.

rationale: Under the assumed execution and signal, follow-ups license documenting what customers report about offline preparation and intended timing. Explicitly labeling retrospective reports and unknowns preserves the limited evidential status required by this claim.
uncertainty: Reports may be inaccurate or incomplete, but the claim concerns their documentation rather than establishing that the reported events occurred.
